types.embedding_query_text: Continent: A large, continuous mass of land on Earth. Also called Landmass, Major land area. Examples: Europe, the continent, this region.

chosen_type.label: Continent
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Continent' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE and its definition.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Mountain
candidates.comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Volcano
candidates.comment: A landform, typically a mountain, with a vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are ejected. Also called active volcano, dormant volcano, volcanic mountain. Examples: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Kilauea.

types.embedding_query_text: Season: One of the four divisions of the year based on changes in weather, ecology, and the amount of daylight. Also called Time of year, Period. Examples: summer.

chosen_type.label: NaturalSeason
chosen_type.definition: One of the four divisions of the year based on changes in weather, ecology, and the amount of daylight.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a natural season; existing 'Season' types refer to media seasons. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for a conceptual time period.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: PodcastSeason
candidates.comment: A PodcastSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason representing a single season of a podcast, used when a podcast is structured into distinct seasons. Also called podcast series season. Examples: "Serial" Season 1, "Lore" Season 3, a specific season of a narrative podcast. Distinct from PodcastSeries, which is the entire podcast collection.

types.embedding_query_text: FieldOfStudy: A branch of knowledge or academic discipline. Also called Discipline, Area of expertise, Subject. Examples: science.

chosen_type.label: Specialty
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Specialty' class, defined as a 'branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise', is a good fit for 'FieldOfStudy' and 'science'.

candidates.label: MedicalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment. Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: MedicalSpecialty
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing any specific branch of medical science or practice, including clinical and allied health specialties. Also called medical field, clinical discipline, healthcare area. Examples: "Cardiology", "Pediatrics", "Oncology", "Physical Therapy", "Dentistry".

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOrganization: An entity responsible for gathering, reporting, and disseminating news and information to the public. Also called Media outlet, News agency, Broadcaster. Examples: Al Jazeera.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'NewsMediaOrganization' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE and its definition.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day, month, and year. Also called Calendar day, Specific day. Examples: 03/07/2026, 2026-07-03.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Date' datatype directly matches the OIE_TYPE and its definition.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: Measurement: A quantity or dimension determined by measuring. Also called Quantity, Dimension, Value. Examples: Temperatures, temperatures.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Quantity' datatype, representing measurable amounts, is the best fit for 'Measurement' and 'Temperatures'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common types or dimensions of measurements. Also called dimension type, measurement category, sizing parameter. Examples: "chest circumference", "inseam length", "screw gauge", "wheel diameter".

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

types.embedding_query_text: State: A particular condition or stage in the existence or development of something. Also called Condition, Status, Situation. Examples: new high, permanent, point of recovery, no longer exist.

chosen_type.label: StatusEnumeration
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'StatusEnumeration' class, representing various status types or states, is the best fit for the general concept of 'State' as a condition or stage.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: ActionStatusType
candidates.comment: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: IncentiveStatus
candidates.comment: IncentiveStatus is an enumeration describing the current status of an incentive, such as whether it is active or expired. Also called incentive state, benefit status, program condition. Examples: 'Active', 'Expired', 'Pending', 'Suspended'.

types.embedding_query_text: WeatherEvent: A specific occurrence or phenomenon related to atmospheric conditions. Also called Meteorological event, Weather phenomenon, Climatic occurrence. Examples: heatwaves, storms, Last Summer's Heatwave, this summer’s heatwave.

chosen_type.label: WeatherEvent
chosen_type.definition: A specific occurrence or phenomenon related to atmospheric conditions.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a weather-related event. 'Event' is the appropriate parent for this type of occurrence.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthCondition: A state of health that deviates from normal functioning, often requiring medical attention. Also called Medical condition, Ailment, Disease. Examples: illness, winter flu.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'MedicalCondition' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE and its definition.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".

types.embedding_query_text: Outcome: The way a thing turns out; a consequence. Also called Result, Consequence, Effect. Examples: deaths, Heat-related mortality, Deaths.

chosen_type.label: Outcome
chosen_type.definition: The way a thing turns out; a consequence or result.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a general 'Outcome' or 'consequence'. 'Thing' is the most appropriate general parent.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

types.embedding_query_text: System: A set of connected things or parts forming a complex whole. Also called Network, Structure, Framework. Examples: infrastructure, Transport, climate system, warning systems.

chosen_type.label: System
chosen_type.definition: A set of connected things or parts forming a complex whole.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents the general concept of a 'System'. 'Thing' is the most appropriate general parent.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: SummerSeason: The warmest season of the year, typically occurring between spring and autumn. Also called Summer period, Warm season. Examples: this summer, Last summer.

chosen_type.label: SummerSeason
chosen_type.definition: The warmest season of the year, typically occurring between spring and autumn.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a natural summer season. It is a specific type of 'NaturalSeason' (minted in E2).

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: RadioSeason
candidates.comment: A RadioSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio series season. Examples: Season 1 of a radio drama, a specific year's collection of a weekly radio show, a themed season of a podcast broadcast on radio.

candidates.label: PodcastSeason
candidates.comment: A PodcastSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason representing a single season of a podcast, used when a podcast is structured into distinct seasons. Also called podcast series season. Examples: "Serial" Season 1, "Lore" Season 3, a specific season of a narrative podcast. Distinct from PodcastSeries, which is the entire podcast collection.

types.embedding_query_text: SeasonPart: A specific segment or portion within a larger season. Also called Part of season, Seasonal segment. Examples: early-summer.

chosen_type.label: SeasonPart
chosen_type.definition: A specific segment or portion within a larger natural season.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a part of a natural season. It is a specific segment of 'NaturalSeason' (minted in E2).

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: One of the seven named days that make up a week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day. Examples: Sunday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'DayOfWeek' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE and its definition.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek

Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: TemperatureValue: A specific numerical reading of temperature. Also called Temperature reading, Heat level. Examples: 40C, 104F, 29.8C, 85.6F.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'QuantitativeValue' class is the best fit for a specific numerical reading of temperature.

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: SteeringPositionValue
candidates.comment: A value indicating the steering position of a vehicle. Also called steering side, driver's side, vehicle control position. Examples: 'LeftHandDriving', 'RightHandDriving'.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory. Also called Nation, State, Realm. Examples: Germany, Czech Republic, Poland, France.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Country' class directly matches the OIE_TYPE and its definition.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: Embassy
candidates.comment: An Embassy is a GovernmentBuilding representing the diplomatic mission of one country in another. Also called consulate, diplomatic mission, high commission. Examples: The U.S. Embassy in London, the French Embassy in Washington D.C., a country's consulate general.

types.embedding_query_text: SettlementType: A classification of a human habitation area, such as a city, town, or village. Also called Habitation area, Populated place, Community type. Examples: one town.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'City' class includes 'town' in its definition, making it the best fit for 'SettlementType' and 'one town'.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. candidates.label: InteractionCounter

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. candidates.label: CarUsageType

types.embedding_query_text: CountryGroup: A collection of multiple countries considered as a single unit or region. Also called Group of nations, Regional bloc. Examples: 12 European countries.

candidates.label: Country

candidates.label: ProductGroup

candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).
